subject: MAP: performance closure sprint & deployment stability benchmarks
summary: Agreement on MAP sprint and evaluation plan. Benchmarks run 5/6–5/7; results show Hosted best for single-request TTFT, Dedicated most predictable under sustained concurrency, Private gives strongest isolation but requires tuning on autoscaler thresholds. Recommended close timeline: contract signature by 2027-05-21 following final SOC2 review.

Technical notes for the bench run:

- Harness: We will run coordinated traffic generators with three profiles: low-latency short prompts (avg tokens 16), medium prompts (avg tokens 64), and long prompts (avg tokens 240).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 400. For each level, run 10k requests or 20 minutes, whichever comes first.
- TTFT measurement: measured at first token emission; include network+runtime impact for Hosted (we'll run from two regions us-west/us-east).
- Isolation tests: for Private we'll simulate noisy co-tenancy by launching background GPU-heavy jobs to verify tail behavior.
- Autoscale check: for Dedicated we will toggle below-threshold load and then spike to test hot-start vs cold-start impact.

Success criteria (suggested):
- Predictability score: standard deviation of p95 across runs < 20% for Dedicated
- Isolation: Private p99 under noisy neighbor < Hosted p99 by at least 15% (if dedicated infra isolation configured)

Subject: Bench results: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (summary + artifacts)

Team / Anna —

Benchmarks completed 5/05–5/07 using the agreed harness. Artifacts: bench_results_hosted_dedicated_private.pdf (summary) and trace_samples_20270507.jsonl (sample traces). Key findings below (full numbers in PDF):

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) — median / p95 / p99 (ms)
- Hosted (us-west): 38 / 82 / 230
- Dedicated (same hw): 44 / 68 / 190
- Private (customer infra snapshot): 52 / 105 / 310

2) Throughput and concurrency (tokens/sec sustained at 95th latency bound):
- Hosted: good single-request TTFT; throughput degrades past 100 concurrent clients; autoscaler provides short bursts but tail increases
- Dedicated: predictable throughput up to 400 concurrent with p95 stable; reserved GPU pools reduce variance
- Private: throughput depends on network/ops tuning; with tuned autoscaler we matched Dedicated for sustained load but saw higher cold-start variability

3) Isolation and predictability:
- Dedicated offered the tightest p95 variance across runs (stddev < 12%).
- Private isolation was best if operator configures strict QoS; otherwise noisy co-tenant simulations increased p99 by ~25%.

4) Autoscaling behavior:
- Hosted: rapid horizontal autoscale but higher cold-start (TTFT spike) during large bursts; mitigation: prefix caching and edge pooling recommended.
- Dedicated: predictable scale with reserved warm pools; recommend burst capacity policy for spikes > 400 concurrent.
- Private: depends on the customer's control plane; we recommend pre-warm hooks and aggressive horizontal scale thresholds for bursty workloads.

5) Recommendation for CometAI:
- If procurement wants fastest time-to-value and lighter ops: Hosted, with prefix/KV caching and a 1–2 minute warm pool for bursts.
- If predictability and SLA-backed latency are top priorities: Dedicated reserved capacity (recommended commit: 3–6 months to tune autoscaler).
- If strict isolation and on-prem constraints drive the decision: Private, but add a tuning window and a rollback clause.

Next steps:
- Stephanie: finalize the MAP + decision rubric and SOW draft (deadline 5/10)
- Rachel: prepare the SOW language for 30-day rollback and pricing options
- Anna: SOC2 checkpoint on 5/18, final signature target 5/21

Attachments: bench_results_hosted_dedicated_private.pdf, trace_samples_20270507.jsonl

—Karthik
